evidence: qwen3-coder: "the discriminant must be positive" and "(a-b)^2 > 0, which means a ≠ b"; gpt-oss-120b: "static ordering works for n<=40"
affordance_in_statement: For the sequence to be valid under a given condition, the quadratic equation z^2 - (C[u] + C[v])z + C[u]C[v] = 0 must have exactly two distinct real roots.
removal_suggestion: Keep the same mathematical constraint but present it indirectly: for each pair, require the cubic z(z^2 - (C[u] + C[v])z + C[u]C[v]) = 0 to have exactly three distinct real roots. Since all C values are positive, this is equivalent, but it hides the immediate discriminant-to-inequality reduction.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the condition as proper 3-coloring and uses recursive backtracking with vertices ordered by decreasing degree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The quadratic-root condition is equivalent to requiring C[u] != C[v], while C values are restricted to {1, 2, 3}.

common_affordance: The root condition transparently reduces to unequal endpoint labels, making the task ordinary 3-coloring.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses exponential recursive coloring without an effective branching heuristic or pruning, causing time-limit exhaustion on hard 3-coloring instances.
Enumerates assignments using a product-style brute force approach over up to 3^40 sequences, which exceeds the time limit.

recommended_edit: Replace the displayed quadratic-root condition with the equivalent cubic-root condition z(z^2 - (C[u] + C[v])z + C[u]C[v]) = 0 having exactly three distinct real roots, preserving the task while defeating solvers that depend on immediately spotting the discriminant (C[u] - C[v])^2.
